div.head: Ps Cn for 34
div.ab: Quodsi canis rabidus momorderit feram, tunc emendet secundum pretium hominis liberalis, quod est duodecies centum solidos, quodsi regalem feram, reus sit maximi criminis.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 626 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)
div.ab: But if a rabid dog has bitten a beast, then let him pay compensation according to the price of a noble man, which is twelve times a hundred shillings; but if a royal beast, let him be guilty of the greatest crime.

note.seg: ca. r. lacking in St Cii

seg.hi: da die Worte z. Th. aus Inst. Cn. entnommen, ist der veränderte Sinn nicht glaublich

note.seg: since the words are partly taken from Inst. Cn., the altered sense is not credible
Si uero fera regalis morsa fuerit, reus Ho
Si uero fera regalis morsa fuerit, reus Ho
vermuthlich der Strafe für Erlegung des Hirsches, d. h. für Villane Todesstrafe; s. o. 19. 25. Vgl. 22bb
presumably (guilty) of the penalty for killing the hart, i.e. for villeins the death penalty; see above 19. 25. Cf. 22 note bb
Verf. scheint überall den Schilling von 12 Pf. zu meinen, missversteht also den Sinn seiner Quelle
The author seems everywhere to mean the shilling of 12 pence, and so misunderstands the sense of his source
